title: Provider selection and boundaries
bodyMarkdown:
## Connect a declared source to one workload

Prerequisites: an operator-approved provider/account, a supported identity profile and a protected policy. First run `cq providers` to inspect what the selected executable implements. Selectors in a document or a provider picker are not proof that the installed authentication/lifecycle combination is supported.

1. Choose the exact source type and resource boundary. For JSON use a policy-relative path and exact top-level string field; for AWS select account/region and exact ARN/name/version; for Azure select tenant/vault/secret/version; for GCP select project/secret/version. Use the provider reference for other supported selectors.
2. Configure only the selected adapter's identity mechanism. Native cloud-reader profiles do not fall back to a developer login; hosted-manager adapters read an operator-provisioned protected token file, not an interactive session.
3. Add a binding whose source identifies that declaration and whose output name is unique within the workload. Check field/version selectors for the chosen provider. A fetched value remains literal; shell/template-looking content is not evaluated.
4. Validate and plan with the selected policy. Exercise an allowed and a denied synthetic case before enabling operational retrieval. A wrong/missing identity, unsupported profile or missing dependency must be repaired explicitly, not bypassed using an administrator's ambient credentials.
5. Enable offline export or publication only when the binding and provider lifecycle permit it. Retrieval permission alone does not allow either operation.

## Interpret provider choices in the preview

The browser source/profile forms store synthetic local metadata. Saving a profile or selecting a provider does not connect to it. Check the source and profile again after local reload/export/restore; actual provider acceptance belongs to native/hosted qualification.

1Password uses an exact service-account `op read` reference, not desktop approval, op run/inject or Environments. Infisical imports/reference expansion stay disabled unless approved. SOPS KMS protects an envelope key; it does not automatically import a secret store. If an upstream read necessarily exposes a whole record/config, split upstream records when consumers need narrower access.
capabilityStatus: Provider support depends on the selected executable, adapter, identity and dependencies. Browser provider/profile choices are local demonstrations and do not connect an account.
